**Refining hierarchical CLA**

**Defining group prefix wires**

**Considering carry stages**

**Defining carry logic**

{
  "candidate_rtl": "module alu_64bit(
    input [63:0] a, b,
    input [2:0] Oper,
    output reg [63:0] sum
);
    wire sub_ab, sub_ba, sub_any;
    wire en_arith, en_or, en_and, en_xor, en_xnor;
    wire [63:0] x, y, axb, p, g;
    wire [63:0] arithmetic_result;
    wire [15:0] pg [0:4];
    wire [15:0] gg [0:4];
    wire [16:0] block_carry;

    assign sub_ab = (Oper == 3'b001);
    assign sub_ba = (Oper == 3'b010);
    assign sub_any = sub_ab | sub_ba;
    assign en_arith = ~Oper[2] & ~(Oper[1] & Oper[0]);
    assign en_or   = (Oper == 3'b011);
    assign en_and  = (Oper == 3'b100);
    assign en_xor  = (Oper == 3'b101);
    assign en_xnor = (Oper == 3'b110);

    assign x = a ^ {64{sub_ba}};
    assign y = b ^ {64{sub_ab}};
    assign axb = a ^ b;
    assign p = axb ^ {64{sub_any}};
    assign g = x & y;
    assign block_carry[0] = sub_any;

    genvar k, s, j;
    generate
        for (k = 0; k < 16; k = k + 1) begin: groups
            assign pg[0][k] = &p[4*k +: 4];
            assign gg[0][k] = g[4*k+3]
                           | (p[4*k+3] & g[4*k+2])
                           | (p[4*k+3] & p[4*k+2] & g[4*k+1])
                           | (p[4*k+3] & p[4*k+2] & p[4*k+1] & g[4*k]);

            assign block_carry[k+1] = gg[4][k]
                                    | (pg[4][k] & sub_any);

            assign arithmetic_result[4*k] = p[4*k] ^ block_carry[k];
            assign arithmetic_result[4*k+1] = p[4*k+1]
                ^ (g[4*k] | (p[4*k] & block_carry[k]));
            assign arithmetic_result[4*k+2] = p[4*k+2]
                ^ (g[4*k+1]
                   | (p[4*k+1] & g[4*k])
                   | (p[4*k+1] & p[4*k] & block_carry[k]));
            assign arithmetic_result[4*k+3] = p[4*k+3]
                ^ (g[4*k+2]
                   | (p[4*k+2] & g[4*k+1])
                   | (p[4*k+2] & p[4*k+1] & g[4*k])
                   | (p[4*k+2] & p[4*k+1] & p[4*k]
                      & block_carry[k]));
        end

        for (s = 0; s < 4; s = s + 1) begin: prefix_stage
            for (j = 0; j < 16; j = j + 1) begin: prefix_bit
                if (j >= (1 << s)) begin: combine
                    assign gg[s+1][j] = gg[s][j]
                        | (pg[s][j] & gg[s][j-(1 << s)]);
                    assign pg[s+1][j] = pg[s][j]
                        & pg[s][j-(1 << s)];
                end else begin: pass_through
                    assign gg[s+1][j] = gg[s][j];
                    assign pg[s+1][j] = pg[s][j];
                end
            end
        end
    endgenerate

    always @(*) begin
        sum = (arithmetic_result & {64{en_arith}})
            | ((a | b) & {64{en_or}})
            | ((a & b) & {64{en_and}})
            | (axb & {64{en_xor}})
            | ((~axb) & {64{en_xnor}});
    end
endmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The original contains three separate 64-bit arithmetic expressions followed by operation selection. Long carry propagation and the arithmetic-result selection network are likely maximum-arrival bottlenecks.",
  "rewrite": "Share one add/subtract datapath: invert b for a-b, invert a for b-a, and inject carry-in one for either subtraction. Use four-bit local carry lookahead and a four-stage parallel-prefix network across sixteen groups. Decode the operation once and combine arithmetic and bitwise results with mutually exclusive masks.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "The explicit logarithmic inter-group carry network is intended to reduce worst-case arithmetic arrival relative to synthesis-generated long carry chains. Sharing arithmetic also reduces the number of wide arithmetic results feeding output selection. Actual timing gain requires the specified mapping and timing evaluation; no measured gain is claimed.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "The prefix network adds carry-combination wiring and gates compared with a ripple adder, while sharing the three arithmetic operations removes duplicated datapaths. This is intended to leave room under the fixed area cap, but mapped area and zero electrical violations remain unverified without running the evaluation flow.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Preserves the module name, port widths, unsigned interpretation, combinational behavior, and all eight operation encodings. Arithmetic outputs are modulo 2^64, including b-a for Oper=010. Oper=111 produces exactly zero. The original internal c_out is unobservable and is omitted; there is no carry output, state, latency, or input assumption."
}
